key_insight: MOSAIC is a two-phase multi-LLM system that can synthesize structured EHR evidence into multidimensional disease-severity phenotypes for type 2 diabetes.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help researchers and clinicians capture severity signals that rule-based scores miss, potentially improving risk stratification and phenotype discovery.
method: Built as an agentic LLM framework with two phases for severity phenotyping.
Tested on synthetic EHR data for type 2 diabetes.
Compared against three algorithmic severity scores and clinical outcomes; open- and closed-weight versions were also benchmarked.
evidence_signal: On SyntheticMass EHR data, open-weight MOSAIC closely matched the proprietary pipeline (weighted kappa 0.773) and showed moderate to fair agreement with existing severity scores, while severity tiers separated mortality and complications significantly.
watch_item: Results were shown in synthetic data and the framework needs external validation before real-world clinical use.
paper_title: Multi-Large Language Model Orchestrated Severity Assessment of Clinical Records (MOSAIC)
